label: Stop 4: The Heineken Brewery and the Rooftop Tour

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay, this is huge. A giant brick building with a red star.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Number 78, Stadhouderskade. The old Heineken brewery.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: It looks like a factory.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It was one. It sits right next to the canal that marks the old edge of the city.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: So it's the actual place where beer was made.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: For over a hundred years. The story starts in 1864.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A young man named Gerard Adriaan Heineken, just twenty-two years old, bought a brewery called De Hooiberg, which means the haystack.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: He bought a brewery at twenty-two.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: With help. His mother put up money.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: And the family had money.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Naturally.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: He soon built a new brewery on this spot, and it began producing in 1867.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The city was growing, and beer was a big business.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the beer is the one with the star.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The red star, yes. That became the trademark, and it's still on every bottle.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: What's special about the beer?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: One thing is the yeast. In the 1880s the company hired a scientist, Doctor Elion, who isolated a pure strain of yeast.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The company calls it the A-yeast, and still uses a descendant of it.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Like a family pet.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Rather like a family pet. And a company secret.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Huh. So a brewery, a hundred years, then?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Then it closed. Making beer here ended in 1988, because the plant was too small for a modern brewery.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The beer moved to bigger sites elsewhere in the country.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And the building became a museum.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A visitor attraction, now called the Heineken Experience.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The tour is the main thing.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And we have the rooftop version.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Yes. Your ticket is for 4:45 PM.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Don't be late, because tours start on the dot.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Details vary, so follow the instructions you were given when you booked.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And what's on top?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: We're not going to describe what we can't confirm.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: What we can say is that the building is one of the tall brick landmarks of the neighborhood, so a roof gives you a view over the south of the city.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And beer.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Tastings are part of the experience, yes.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Please enjoy them responsibly, and get home safely.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Fair. Okay, but you promised spooky, and I think there's something here.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: There is. It's not a legend. It's real, and it's serious, so we're going to talk about it plainly.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: In November 1983, the owner of the company, Freddy Heineken, was kidnapped, together with his driver, Ab Doderer.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: They were taken from the street near the company's offices and held captive for about three weeks.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: By whom?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: A group of Dutch criminals. They demanded a very large ransom, around 35 million guilders at the time, which was one of the largest ransoms ever paid in the world.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: And they were freed?

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Yes. Both men were released at the end of November.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: The kidnappers were later caught, and several were convicted.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: That must have been terrifying.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It was. The case is still remembered here as one of the most shocking crimes in modern Dutch history.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Thank you for telling it straight.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: It's part of the story of the place.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: We'll say no more.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: Okay. Let's gather ourselves. Enjoy the tour.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Pause here for as long as the tour takes.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: About an hour and a half should be plenty, and then, dinner.

units.speaker: Anna
units.text: I'll be the one humming.

units.speaker: Ben
units.text: Of course you will.
